notes:
Particular-vote sequence on a tax-evasion bill, articles 3 to 6. 22 printed labels, 5 stenographer lines, no headings and no back-links or other furniture in this fragment.

Typography: three consecutive paragraphs in the middle of the fragment (article 5: the chair's two lines and the vote note between them) are set WITHOUT the surrounding <FONT FACE="Times New Roman"> wrapper that every other paragraph carries, and use a real em dash '—' where the rest of the fragment uses a double hyphen '--'. I checked the raw file (data/raw/senado/taquigraficas/2000-06-07_r22_ORDINARIA.html, around byte 228000): the same anomaly is there, so it is the chamber's own patched-in passage, not damage introduced when the fragment was cut. The two labels in that patch are recorded with the em dash, as printed. The fragment file is UTF-8 while the raw file is cp1252; that is the only difference between them.

Counting rule applied: every printed label is a start, including the chair's repeated announcements around a vote note ('Se va a votar' / note / 'Queda aprobado') and Villarroel's three labelled segments broken up by the two 'Varios señores senadores hablan a la vez' interruptions. This is the hard case in this fragment: rule 2 of the brief could be read as merging a speaker's labelled resumption after a note into one turn, but the existing gold set for the PDF era does not read it that way — reference/gold/gold_2004-04-28_p24.json lists four separate 'Sr. Presidente. —' starts across two electronic votes — so I followed the printed label. Unlabelled continuation paragraphs inside Villarroel's and Yoma's long speeches are NOT listed, which is what rule 2 governs.

The chair's two 'Queda aprobado con 47 votos por la afirmativa sobre 50 senadores' announcements (articles 4 and 5) are verbatim identical; they are two distinct turns, not a duplication introduced here. Nothing in this fragment is an inserted document; all of it is floor speech.
